# nsconv — NetStream Converter

**Huawei NetStream in, clean IPFIX / NetFlow out — for Illumio FlowLink and other collectors.**

<!-- generated by scripts/publish-public.sh; latest version: 0.1.0-rc1 -->

nsconv runs next to Illumio FlowLink on a RHEL/Rocky/Alma 8 or 9 host. It receives NetStream (NetFlow v5, v9 and
IPFIX with Huawei's quirks) from your switches and re-exports clean IPFIX, NetFlow v9 or v5 that FlowLink can
ingest, keeping each switch's own source address. One static binary, one sandboxed systemd service.

```
Huawei switches ──NetStream (UDP 9996)──▶ nsconv ──IPFIX (UDP 4739)──▶ FlowLink ──HTTPS──▶ Illumio PCE
```

**[Documentation](https://roschereric.github.io/netstream-converter/)** — operator guide, test kit and
switch capture kit, in English and Spanish · **[Download 0.1.0-rc1](releases/0.1.0-rc1/)**

> **0.1.0-rc1 is a test build.** Use it in a lab or POC, not in production yet.

## Download and verify

[`releases/0.1.0-rc1/`](releases/0.1.0-rc1/) holds static Linux binaries (x86_64, aarch64), RPMs for EL8/EL9,
a CycloneDX SBOM, `SHA256SUMS` and [`NOTES.md`](releases/0.1.0-rc1/NOTES.md). The artifacts are not signed:

```
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

## Install

RPM (recommended):

```
sudo dnf install ./nsconv-0.1.0~rc1-1.x86_64.rpm
sudo nsconvctl config set input.huawei.allow '["198.51.100.11"]'      # example switch IP
sudo nsconvctl config set output.flowlink.target 127.0.0.1:4739       # example FlowLink address
sudo systemctl enable --now nsconv
sudo nsconvctl status                                                   # or: sudo nsconvctl tui
```

Binary only: `chmod +x nsconvctl-0.1.0-rc1-x86_64-linux && sudo ./nsconvctl-0.1.0-rc1-x86_64-linux install --enable`.

Then point FlowLink's IPFIX consumer at port 4739 with `remote_addrs` set to the switch IPs. The operator guide
covers FlowLink, firewalld, SELinux and the Huawei side.

## Try it without a switch

```
nsconvctl tui --demo                     # the terminal UI with demo data
nsconvctl decode capture.pcap            # decode a NetStream capture and print the flows
```
